  "core_problem": "Can we learn explicit spatial affordance representations within an end-to-end Vision-Language-Action model without any affordance annotations or external supervision signals, by jointly exploiting (1) instruction paraphrase invariance — semantically equivalent instructions must activate identical spatial affordance regions — and (2) cross-object affordance transfer — objects with similar functional parts must exhibit similar affordance patterns for the same interaction type — producing interpretable intermediate representations that improve manipulation success, paraphrase robustness, and zero-shot generalization to novel objects beyond what action-level invariance methods (RSS, LangForce), supervised spatial affordance approaches (PALM, CoA-VLA), spatial grounding with web-scale data (ST4VLA), 3D teacher-based alignment (Spatial Forcing), or standalone affordance modules (INTRA, AffordanceSAM) can achieve — all without the annotation pipelines, web-scale grounding data, simulator labels, or foundation model teachers that existing spatial methods require?",
  "opportunity": "Recent work has firmly established that spatial representations within VLAs improve manipulation — ST4VLA (ICLR 2026) uses point/box/trajectory spatial priors from web-scale grounding data achieving 95.9% on LIBERO, Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026) aligns intermediate VLA embeddings with a 3D foundation model (VGGT) achieving 98.5% LIBERO average (current SOTA), PALM (CVPR 2026) integrates 4 supervised affordance types achieving 91.8% on LIBERO-Long, and SG-VLA (March 2026) co-trains affordance decoders with simulator-extracted labels. However, all these methods require external supervision: ST4VLA needs web-scale grounding data (RefCOCO, LLaVA-OneVision); PALM requires a semi-automated annotation pipeline (GroundingDINO + SAM + SpatialVLM + RoboPoint + CoTracker); SG-VLA depends on simulator ground-truth labels (grasp states, segmentation masks); and Spatial Forcing requires a pretrained 3D foundation model as teacher. This supervision dependence creates a critical scaling bottleneck — deploying to new environments, tasks, or real-world settings without simulators requires re-annotation or re-collection of grounding data. Meanwhile, LIBERO-Para (arXiv 2603.28301, March 2026) reveals that VLAs suffer 22-52 percentage point drops under simple paraphrasing with 80-96% of failures at the planning level — and none of the above spatial methods (ST4VLA, PALM, SG-VLA, Spatial Forcing) have been evaluated on LIBERO-Para, leaving paraphrase robustness as an untested dimension for spatial VLA methods. The context-dependent affordance study (arXiv 2603.04419) confirms that stable latent affordance factors persist despite >90% lexical drift across contexts, suggesting spatial affordance structure is exploitable as a free self-supervision signal from paraphrases alone. OpenVLA-OFT achieves 97.1% on LIBERO with LoRA fine-tuning in ~10-15 hours on a single A100, providing a compute-efficient backbone.",
  "landscape": "**Spatial representations in VLAs (supervised/teacher-based)**: ST4VLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2602.10109) uses spatial priors (point, box, trajectory) from web-scale grounding pre-training (RefCOCO, LLaVA-OneVision) followed by spatially guided action post-training, achieving 95.9% LIBERO average (92.6% Long) and emergent paraphrase robustness in real-world (52% on novel instructions by attribute) — the closest spatial VLA, but requires web-scale grounding data not available in new domains and does not explicitly learn affordance maps. Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.12276) aligns intermediate VLA visual embeddings with 3D representations from VGGT, achieving 98.5% LIBERO average (96.0% Long) with 3.8x training speedup — a plug-and-play approach demonstrating that intermediate spatial alignment improves VLAs, but requires a pretrained 3D foundation model as teacher with no learned affordance structure.   "approach": "We propose AffordInvar, which augments OpenVLA-OFT with a lightweight spatial affordance decoder trained jointly with the VLA via LoRA using two complementary self-supervised signals — requiring no affordance annotations, web-scale grounding data, simulator labels, or foundation model teachers. **Architecture**: The affordance decoder takes intermediate features from the VLA's 18th transformer layer (out of 32), which retain spatial structure before the final action-prediction layers. The decoder consists of 3 transposed convolution blocks (each: ConvTranspose2d 4x4 stride 2, GroupNorm, GELU) upsampling from 16x16 to 128x128 resolution, with text conditioning via the instruction embedding projected through a linear layer and channel-wise multiplied at each block (~8M parameters total, <0.12% of VLA backbone). Output is a sigmoid-activated 128x128 affordance heatmap. **Self-supervised signal 1 — Paraphrase invariance (L_consist)**: For each training episode, Qwen 3 generates K=3 semantically equivalent instruction paraphrases offline. During training, each paraphrase-image pair is processed through the VLA, and a symmetric KL divergence loss enforces identical affordance heatmaps across all K+1 instruction variants: L_consist = (1/C(K+1,2)) sum_{i<j} KL(h_i || h_j), extending SelfEQ's visual grounding consistency (CVPR 2024) from general VLM grounding to the VLA affordance domain. Unlike RSS which applies paraphrase averaging at the action logit level, we enforce consistency at the intermediate spatial representation level, providing richer structured learning signal. Unlike ST4VLA's emergent robustness from web-scale spatial pre-training, we explicitly optimize for instruction invariance. **Self-supervised signal 2 — Cross-object affordance transfer (L_transfer)**: Episodes with semantically similar instructions (cosine similarity > 0.85 on instruction embeddings) but different target objects are mined as positive pairs; episodes with the same object but different interaction types serve as negatives. A contrastive InfoNCE loss on spatially-normalized affordance features encourages interaction-specific (not object-specific) affordance representations, enabling zero-shot transfer to novel objects — inspired by INTRA's interaction-relationship contrastive learning but operating on VLA-internal features with free-form instructions rather than predefined interaction labels. **Affordance-action integration**: The affordance heatmap is bilinearly downsampled to the action feature resolution and applied as an element-wise gate: action_features = action_features * sigma(W_g * affordance_features + b_g), where W_g is a learned linear projection (~0.5M parameters). This is architecturally similar to SG-VLA's auxiliary decoder approach but with a key difference: our decoder is trained entirely self-supervised while SG-VLA requires simulator ground truth for each auxiliary task. **Entropy regularization**: H_entropy = -lambda_H sum h_i log(h_i), preventing degenerate uniform or collapsed heatmaps. **Total loss**: L = L_action + alpha*L_consist + beta*L_transfer + lambda_H*H_entropy, where L_action is OpenVLA-OFT's continuous L1 action regression loss. **Evaluation**: (1) Manipulation success on LIBERO-Long (10 tasks, standard) and LIBERO-Para (paraphrase robustness, measuring PRIDE score) — we will be the first to evaluate a spatial affordance VLA method on LIBERO-Para; (2) Zero-shot generalization to held-out object categories within LIBERO; (3) Held-out interaction type generalization: train without all 'opening' tasks and test on them, plus creative rephrasings via Qwen 3 using novel interaction vocabulary (e.g., 'unfasten the container' instead of 'open the drawer') to test whether affordance representations generalize to unseen interaction semantics; (4) Affordance transfer evaluation with fine-tuning protocol: (a) zero-shot application of the VLA-learned affordance decoder on AGD20K/UMD as an exploratory experiment assessing cross-domain affordance quality, and (b) fine-tuning only the affordance decoder on AGD20K while freezing the VLA backbone, testing whether VLA-learned representations provide useful initialization vs. training from scratch — this addresses the large sim-to-real domain gap; (5) Qualitative affordance map visualization and contact-point prediction accuracy on held-out LIBERO episodes. **Baselines**: (a) OpenVLA-OFT (vanilla, no affordance) — 97.1% LIBERO standard; (b) OpenVLA-OFT + RSS-style action-level paraphrase invariance (our reimplementation); (c) OpenVLA-OFT + Spatial Forcing (intermediate 3D alignment with VGGT teacher) — 98.5% LIBERO average; (d) PALM (semi-automated affordance annotation) — 91.8% LIBERO-Long; (e) ST4VLA (web-scale spatial grounding) — 95.9% LIBERO average; (f) INTRA affordance maps + OpenVLA-OFT policy (two-stage); (g) CoA-VLA (supervised affordance). Key comparison axis: standard LIBERO performance may be competitive but not necessarily SOTA (Spatial Forcing at 98.5% is hard to beat without 3D teachers); our primary advantage claims are on (i) LIBERO-Para paraphrase robustness where explicit invariance training should outperform emergent robustness, (ii) zero-shot novel object/interaction generalization where annotation-free affordance transfer should outperform annotation-dependent methods in out-of-distribution settings, and (iii) annotation efficiency — competitive performance without any affordance labels, web-scale data, or foundation model teachers. **Key hypotheses**: (a) Explicit paraphrase invariance at the spatial affordance level provides better PRIDE scores on LIBERO-Para than ST4VLA's emergent robustness from spatial grounding or RSS's action-level invariance; (b) Self-supervised cross-object affordance transfer enables superior zero-shot generalization to novel objects compared to methods that learn object-specific supervised affordance features (PALM, SG-VLA); (c) Despite requiring no external supervision, AffordInvar achieves within 2-3 percentage points of supervised spatial methods (PALM, ST4VLA) on standard LIBERO, demonstrating that self-supervision closes most of the gap; (d) VLA-learned affordance representations provide useful initialization for downstream affordance benchmarks, demonstrated by faster convergence when fine-tuning the decoder on AGD20K vs. training from scratch.",

## Reviewer feedback (round 5)
Issues: ["MODERATE RISK — Self-supervised signal quality: The proposal acknowledges this risk (Round 4 feedback) and includes entropy regularization + a contingency plan (trajectory contact points as lightweight supervision). However, the specific analysis requested in Round 4 — what fraction of Qwen-3 paraphrases create genuine spatial ambiguity vs. trivial synonym substitution in LIBERO's templated instructions — is discussed conceptually but not operationalized as a pre-experiment diagnostic. Running this analysis before committing to full training would save substantial compute if the signal proves weak.", "MODERATE RISK — Hypothesis (c) reframing: The proposal now correctly positions the primary advantage on LIBERO-Para and OOD generalization rather than standard LIBERO competition, but the hypothesis still states 'within 2-3 percentage points of supervised spatial methods' on standard LIBERO. Given OpenVLA-OFT already achieves 97.1% without any affordance and Spatial Forcing achieves ~98.5%, the ceiling improvement from adding self-supervised affordance on standard LIBERO may be negligible or negative (added complexity). Consider explicitly hypothesizing that standard LIBERO performance should be maintained (not degraded) rather than improved, with gains concentrated on OOD/paraphrase conditions.", "MINOR — UAD (arXiv 2506.09284, Stanford, June 2025) is not cited: While UAD is a standalone affordance module (not end-to-end VLA), it represents the closest work on 'unsupervised/annotation-free affordance for robot manipulation' and should be acknowledged in the landscape discussion to preempt reviewer concerns about novelty.", "MINOR — Spatial Forcing 98.5% LIBERO average not independently verified with exact numbers: The proposal cites 98.5% average and 96.0% Long, but the project page and abstract don't surface exact per-suite numbers. While this doesn't affect the proposal's validity (the approximate SOTA status is confirmed), having verified source numbers for the camera-ready version would strengthen the comparison.", "MINOR — The 'first spatial VLA evaluated on LIBERO-Para' claim is strong but should be hedged: LIBERO-Para was published March 2026 and it's plausible that concurrent work may evaluate spatial VLAs on it before this paper is submitted (AAAI 2027 deadline ~July 2026).", "Quality gate: avg score 3.8 < 4.0 — idea needs significant improvement"]
Feedback: This proposal has matured significantly over 5 rounds and now presents a well-differentiated, technically detailed, and feasible research plan. The gap is independently verified as real. Three minor improvements for the final submission: (1) Add UAD (Stanford, 2506.09284) to landscape — it's the closest annotation-free affordance work and reviewers will find it. Your differentiation: end-to-end VLA integration vs. standalone module. (2) Reframe hypothesis (c) from 'within 2-3pp of supervised methods' to 'maintains OpenVLA-OFT baseline performance on standard LIBERO while achieving superior LIBERO-Para PRIDE and OOD generalization' — this is more defensible given the 97-98.5% saturation range. (3) Hedge the 'first spatial VLA on LIBERO-Para' claim slightly — say 'to our knowledge' since 2+ months remain before AAAI deadline.
Scores too low (avg 3.8/5). All ideas must achieve avg >= 4.0 to pass. Strengthen novelty, feasibility, clarity, and impact.

## Instructions
- Think in two phases: FIRST reconsider the problem framing (core_problem / opportunity / landscape) if the reviewer flagged issues there, THEN revise the method (approach / resource_estimate / key_references). Do not jump straight to fixing the method if the underlying problem framing needs correction.
- Address each issue specifically.

## 深度调研要求（每一轮修订都必须执行）

不要简单地'打补丁'——每一轮修订都是重新审视和深化这个 idea 的机会。

1. **深度搜索**：针对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，建议用 2-3 种不同的搜索查询调研。
   - 搜索最新的相关论文（arXiv, conference proceedings）
   - 搜索 benchmark/leaderboard 确认当前 SOTA
   - 搜索可能遗漏的相关工作和 concurrent work

2. **深度阅读**：用 WebFetch 实际阅读找到的关键论文的 abstract 和方法部分，
   不要只依赖搜索摘要。形成你自己对领域现状的独立判断。

3. **深度思考**：在修订之前，先独立思考以下问题：
   - 这个 idea 的核心假设是否仍然成立？
   - reviewer 的批评是否揭示了更深层的问题？
   - 有没有更好的 framing 或 approach 来解决同一个核心问题？
   - 修订后的 idea 相比上一版有什么本质性的改进？

4. **避免表面修订**：如果你发现自己只是在换措辞或补充细节而没有实质改进，
   考虑是否需要 major revision 或 pivot。反复的 minor fix 不会拯救一个根基有问题的 idea。

## 针对 Review 意见的定向搜索

对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，执行以下搜索流程：

1. **如果 reviewer 说'已有类似工作'**：
   - 搜索 reviewer 提到的论文，用 WebFetch 实际阅读
   - 搜索该论文的 cited-by，找到后续跟进工作
   - 明确你的 idea 与这些工作的差异化点——如果差异化不够，必须 pivot

2. **如果 reviewer 说'SOTA 过时'**：
   - 用 Papers With Code 查看当前排行榜
   - 搜索过去 6 个月的最新方法
   - 更新你的 landscape 和 baseline

3. **如果 reviewer 说'可行性有问题'**：
   - 搜索类似规模实验的实际成本和时间线
   - 搜索 GitHub 上是否有可复用的实现
   - 搜索相关数据集/模型的可获取性

4. **如果 reviewer 说'novelty 不足'**：
   - 对核心方法尽量做 3-5 种不同关键词组合的搜索
   - 搜索相邻领域是否有类似思路
   - 如果确实 novelty 不足，考虑 major revision 或 pivot

- Use WebSearch to find updated information if the reviewer flagged outdated claims.
- You have full freedom in how much to change:
  - Minor fix: if only specific details are wrong, correct them and keep everything else.

# UAD: Unsupervised Affordance Distillation - Analysis

## Full Abstract
"Understanding fine-grained object affordances is imperative for robots to manipulate objects in unstructured environments given open-ended task instructions. However, existing methods of visual affordance predictions often rely on manually annotated data or conditions only on a predefined set of tasks. We introduce UAD (Unsupervised Affordance Distillation), a method for distilling affordance knowledge from foundation models into a task-conditioned affordance model without any manual annotations. By leveraging the complementary strengths of large vision models and vision-language models, UAD automatically annotates a large-scale dataset with detailed <instruction, visual affordance> pairs. Training only a lightweight task-conditioned decoder atop frozen features, UAD exhibits notable generalization to in-the-wild robotic scenes and to various human activities, despite only being trained on rendered objects in simulation. Using affordance provided by UAD as the observation space, we show an imitation learning policy that demonstrates promising generalization to unseen object instances, object categories, and even variations in task instructions after training on as few as 10 demonstrations."

UAD distills affordance knowledge from foundation models (vision and vision-language models) into a task-conditioned decoder without manual supervision.

**Zero manual annotations** - the system auto-generates training data by leveraging large pre-trained vision and vision-language models.

The document does not specify explicit benchmark names, only mentioning evaluation on "in-the-wild robotic scenes" and "various human activities."

## Key Results
The approach generalizes to unseen object instances, categories, and task instruction variations using only 10 demonstrations with imitation learning.

## Integration Architecture
**Standalone affordance module** - UAD functions as an observation space provider for downstream imitation learning policies, not as an end-to-end VLA component.

## SelfEQ: Improved Visual Grounding through Self-Consistent Explanations

The work proposes a strategy for augmenting existing text-image datasets with paraphrases using a large language model, and develops SelfEQ, a weakly-supervised strategy on visual explanation maps for paraphrases that encourages self-consistency.

**Key Methodology:**

For an input textual phrase, the method attempts to generate a paraphrase and finetune the model so that the phrase and paraphrase map to the same region in the image. More specifically, the SelfEQ tuning is based on the premise that if a vision-language model is identified as self-consistent, the attention maps produced for both the text and its equivalent paraphrase should yield nearly identical results, achieved through a simple mean squared error loss over the produced heatmaps so that their ℓ2 distance is minimized.

**How SelfEQ Differs:**

SelfEQ encourages consistent visual explanations for different prompts on the same image by relying on automatically generated paraphrases. This is distinct from other approaches that focus on different premises.

**Results:**

The work shows that the localization "grounding" abilities of vision-and-language models can be further improved by fine-tuning for self-consistent visual explanations.

This research was published at CVPR 2024 and addresses weakly-supervised visual grounding without requiring box annotations.

## Affordance Field Intervention (AFI)

Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown great performance in robotic manipulation by mapping visual observations and language instructions directly to actions. However, they remain brittle under distribution shifts: when test scenarios change, VLAs often reproduce memorized trajectories instead of adapting to the updated scene, which is a failure mode referred to as the "Memory Trap".

Affordance Field Intervention (AFI) is a lightweight hybrid framework that uses 3D Spatial Affordance Fields (SAFs) as an on-demand plug-in to guide VLA behavior.

## 3D Spatial Affordance Fields (SAFs)

3D Spatial Affordance Fields (SAFs) can provide a geometric representation that highlights where interactions are physically feasible, offering explicit cues about regions the robot should approach or avoid.

## How AFI Works

The system includes memory trap detection by monitoring end-effector velocity and distance to target, and upon detection, the robot rolls back to the historical position with lowest SAF cost before grasping attempts.

This research was published in December 2025, representing recent advances in combining spatial reasoning with vision-language-action models for improved robotic manipulation.
